# Paper 3: ResNet (2015)

*Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition* · Module 1 — Optimization and depth · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#paper-3)

## Study approach
Separate vanishing gradients (fixed by BatchNorm) from the degradation problem (deeper plain nets have higher training error). Why $F(x) = H(x) - x$ is easier than learning identity.

## Interview hooks
"What training failure do residuals prevent?" (asked in the Transformer section too).

## Break-it experiments
1. **HAND→AGENT** — `out = block(x) + alpha * x` with alpha ∈ {0, 1}, 20- vs 56-layer on CIFAR-10; watch the 56-layer plain net lose.
   - Code: `experiments/exp1_with_alpha_0_1_20_vs_56_layer_on.ipynb`
2. **HAND→AGENT** — Zero-init the last BatchNorm γ in each block so blocks start as identity (the same trick reappears in #20 DiT).
   - Code: `experiments/exp2_zero_init_the_last_batchnorm_in.ipynb`
